text:
mari: FYI helm upgrade for release/redwood-gpupool in eu-west-1 failed and left resources stuck in Terminating. upgrade rolled back but GitOps pipeline is still blocked by CRD finalizers. logs attached below. :grimacing:

ben: Can you paste the error from the helm hook?

mari: from tiller logs: 
```
Hook job "post-upgrade-cleanup" exited 1: failed to remove legacy finalizers: timeout waiting for CRD conversion webhook
```

mari: and `kubectl get gpupool -A -o yaml` shows finalizers on several objects: 
```
metadata:
  finalizers:
  - gpupool.k8s.redwood.io/cleanup
  deletionTimestamp: "2024-04-25T14:02:23Z"
```

ben: OK that matches. The post-upgrade hook tried to call the conversion webhook to migrate objects, webhook timed out -> objects stuck deleting -> helm hook can't complete -> helm rollout stuck.

ben: Quick workaround: patch the CRD to remove the finalizer locally (manual) then continue the rollback. e.g. 
```
kubectl patch gpupool <name> -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":null}}' --type=merge -n <ns>
kubectl patch crd gpupools.gpu.redwood.io -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":null}}' --type=merge
```

mari: did that for 3 resources, helm finished. But GitOps (flux) still sees drift because webhook keeps flaking for a subset in the eu-west control plane.

tariq: We need root cause: why cron conversion webhook timed out only in eu-west? Any network egress or nodeport issue? Could be nodepool autoscale drained the webhook pods during upgrade window.

sre-oncall: Confirmed webhook pods were OOMKilled around the same time due to a surge in reconciliation after the gpupool resize. kube-events show bursts of List/Watch followed by CPU throttling.

mari: Also saw a spike in GPU provisioning requests. The autoscaler bumped up nodes but because the webhook uses a stateful cache warmup it hit a thundering herd and crashed.

ben: Short-term mitigation: increase webhook replicas and add readiness probe so helm hook waits until webhook is healthy. Also add a fail-open path in the hook: if conversion fails after N retries, schedule a post-rollout async-cleaner instead of blocking upgrade.

tariq: For the longer term: two proposals:
- make preinstall/postupgrade hooks idempotent and non-blocking (i.e., don't hold helm hook lock while doing long conversions)
- add an operator-runner job that runs in a separate controller with leader-election to migrate finalizers offline

mari: +1. Also can we add a Canary rollout guard in the GitOps pipeline to avoid full fleet upgrades when webhook health is degraded?

sre-oncall: Good idea. We should gate helm upgrades by webhook/CRD health checks. Add a pipeline step that fails fast with a clear message so humans don't have to rediscover finalizers after the fact.

ben: I'll open a quick PR to: bump webhook HPA min=2, add readiness probe, and change the postupgrade hook to enqueue work to a Job that times out quickly (30s) and records migration status to a k8s Condition, not block helm.

mari: Thanks — created an incident ticket and linked PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/412 :eyes:

deploy-bot: Deployment queued: infra/patch/webhook-stability -> staging. Runbook: if CRD finalizers are observed again, run `kubectl get gpupool -A -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.metadata.deletionTimestamp)'` then follow manual-finalizer cleanup steps.

tariq: Also flagging cost note: orphaned gpupool resources prevented node scale-down in eu-west for ~3 hours which added ~0.6 vGPU-hours. Not massive but trending up. We should include that in postmortem.

mari: I'll draft the postmortem and include suggested automation. For now patch rolling to staging. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
